title: Annotated Code of Maryland, Labor and Employment Article, Title 11, Subtitle 3 - Reduction in Operations (Economic Stabilization Act)
verified_how: Fetched the section page for Article - Labor and Employment, § 11-301: live text opening 'In this subtitle the following words have the meanings indicated', defining 'employee', 'employer', 'permanent', 'reduction in operations' and 'workplace' - i.e. the definitional section of Maryland's mass-layoff and plant-closing notice statute. Served with enactments=false; no as-at date printed. Also fetched § 3-505 in the same article, live text opening 'Except as provided in subsection (b) of this section, each employer shall pay an employee...' requiring all wages earned before termination to be paid on or before the regular payment date, with a limited written-policy exception for accrued leave.
notes: Maryland's mini-WARN: 60 days' notice of a reduction in operations, mandatory since 2020 (it was voluntary before), enforced by the Division of Labor and Industry. Maryland does not mandate severance pay itself - §11-304 concerns continuation of benefits; federal WARN (29 U.S.C. 2101) applies in parallel. Final-wage duty on separation is Md. Code, Lab. & Empl. § 3-505, verified above. Unemployment insurance is Title 8 of the same article.
